title: Units, Dimensions & Measurement
excerpt: Comprehensive study notes covering SI Base Units, Derived Units, Dimensional Formulae, and Significant Figures for SSC CGL & CHSL.
content:
🎯 Chapter Overview & SSC Weightage

This chapter forms the cornerstone of Physics in all SSC examinations (CGL, CHSL, CPO, MTS). On average, 1 to 2 direct questions are asked every year regarding SI units, derived physical quantities, or dimensional formulas.

1. Physical Quantities & The SI System

Any quantity that can be measured directly or indirectly is termed a Physical Quantity. The International System of Units (SI) establishes 7 Fundamental (Base) Units and 2 Supplementary Units.

Base Physical Quantity SI Unit Symbol Dimensional Symbol
Length (लंबाई) Meter (मीटर) m [L]
Mass (द्रव्यमान) Kilogram (किलोग्राम) kg [M]
Time (समय) Second (सेकंड) s [T]
Electric Current (विद्युत धारा) Ampere (एम्पीयर) A [A] or [I]
Thermodynamic Temperature (ताप) Kelvin (केल्विन) K [K] or [θ]
Luminous Intensity (ज्योति तीव्रता) Candela (कैंडेला) cd [cd]
Amount of Substance (पदार्थ की मात्रा) Mole (मोल) mol [mol]

💡 Supplementary Units:

  • Plane Angle (समतल कोण): Radian (rad) — Dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰]
  • Solid Angle (ठोस कोण): Steradian (sr) — Dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰]

2. High-Yield Derived Quantities & Formulas

Derived quantities are formed by combining base quantities through algebraic multiplication or division.

⚡ Frequently Asked in SSC Shifts

• Force (बल): F = m × a  →  SI Unit: Newton (N)  |  Dimensions: [M L T⁻²]

• Work / Energy (कार्य / ऊर्जा): W = F × d  →  SI Unit: Joule (J)  |  Dimensions: [M L² T⁻²]

• Power (शक्ति): P = W / t  →  SI Unit: Watt (W)  |  Dimensions: [M L² T⁻³]

• Pressure (दाब / प्रतिबल): P = F / A  →  SI Unit: Pascal (Pa) or N/m²  |  Dimensions: [M L⁻¹ T⁻²]

• Universal Gravitational Constant (G): SI Unit: N·m²/kg²  |  Dimensions: [M⁻¹ L³ T⁻²]

3. Important Multiplier Prefixes

SSC frequently tests metric prefixes in scientific measurement questions:

  • Nano (n): 10⁻⁹ meter
  • Micro (μ): 10⁻⁶ meter
  • Milli (m): 10⁻³ meter
  • Kilo (k): 10³
  • Mega (M): 10⁶
  • Giga (G): 10⁹
  • Tera (T): 10¹²

🔥 SSC PYQ Trend Alert: Questions like "1 Light Year is the unit of?" are repeated every few shifts. Remember: Light Year (प्रकाश वर्ष) is a unit of Distance, NOT Time! (1 Light Year ≈ 9.46 × 10¹⁵ m).

title: Preamble & Borrowed Sources of Indian Constitution
hindi_title: संविधान की प्रस्तावना एवं विदेशी स्रोत
excerpt: Key phrases in the Preamble, 42nd Amendment changes, and country-wise borrowed features of the world's longest written constitution.
content:
1. The Preamble (प्रस्तावना)

The Preamble is based on the 'Objective Resolution' drafted and moved by Pt. Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946 and unanimously adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 January 1947.

42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976: Added three new words to the Preamble: Socialist (समाजवादी), Secular (पंथनिरपेक्ष), and Integrity (अखंडता). The Preamble has been amended only ONCE till date.

2. Major Borrowed Features (विदेशी स्रोत)

Country / Act Borrowed Features in Indian Constitution
Govt. of India Act 1935 Federal Scheme, Office of Governor, Judiciary, Public Service Commissions (UPSC), Emergency provisions.
United Kingdom (UK) Parliamentary form of Government, Rule of Law, Single Citizenship, Bicameralism, Cabinet System, Prerogative Writs.
United States (USA) Fundamental Rights (Part III), Judicial Review, Independence of Judiciary, Impeachment of President, Removal of SC/HC Judges, Preamble concept.
Ireland Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP - Part IV), Nomination of 12 members to Rajya Sabha, Method of President's election.
Australia Concurrent List, Joint Sitting of both Houses of Parliament (Article 108), Freedom of trade and commerce.
USSR (Now Russia) Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), Ideals of Justice (Social, Economic, Political) in Preamble.
South Africa Procedure for Constitutional Amendment (Article 368), Election of Rajya Sabha members.

title: Percentage & Fraction Equivalence Shortcuts
hindi_title: प्रतिशत एवं भिन्न मान: शॉर्ट ट्रिक व मास्टर शीट
excerpt: Master the 1/1 to 1/20 fraction-to-percentage table, successive percentage changes, and AB rule tricks for lightning-fast calculations in SSC CGL.
content:
1. The Sacred Fraction-to-Percentage Table

2. Successive Percentage Formula (AB Formula)

Net Effective Change = (A + B + AB/100)%

Use positive sign for increase/profit and negative sign for decrease/discount.

Example: If price increases by 20% and consumption increases by 10%, Net expenditure increase = 20 + 10 + (20 × 10)/100 = 32%.

3. Product Constancy (A × B = Constant) Rule

If consumption decreases so expenditure stays constant when price rises:

If Price increases by a / b, Consumption must decrease by a / (a + b).

Example: Sugar price rises by 25% (¼). Then consumption must decrease by 1 / (1 + 4) = ⅕ = 20% to maintain same monthly budget!

title: Kinematics & Newton's Laws of Motion
hindi_title: गति एवं न्यूटन के गति के नियम
excerpt: Equations of motion, scalar vs vector quantities, Newton's 3 laws, momentum conservation, and frictional force concepts simplified.
content:
🎯 Chapter Overview

Kinematics deals with the motion of bodies without considering the causes of motion, while Dynamics (Newton's Laws) explains the forces causing motion.

1. Kinematic Equations of Linear Motion

For uniform acceleration along a straight line:

1. Velocity-Time Relation: v = u + at

2. Position-Time Relation: s = ut + ½at²

3. Velocity-Position Relation: v² = u² + 2as

Where: u = initial velocity, v = final velocity, a = uniform acceleration, t = time, s = displacement.

2. Newton's Three Laws of Motion

First Law (Law of Inertia / जड़त्व का नियम):

A body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion in a straight line unless compelled by an external unbalanced force. Inertia depends directly on the mass of the object.

Practical Examples: Passengers leaning backward when a bus starts suddenly; shaking branches to make fruits fall.

Second Law (Law of Force / संवेग परिवर्तन का नियम):

The rate of change of linear momentum is directly proportional to the applied force: F = dp/dt = m × a.

Practical Examples: A cricket fielder pulls his hands backwards while catching a fast ball to increase impact time, thereby reducing the impulsive force.

Third Law (Action-Reaction / क्रिया-प्रतिक्रिया का नियम):

To every action, there is always an equal and opposite reaction acting on two different bodies: F₁₂ = -F₂₁.

Practical Examples: Rocket propulsion, recoil of a gun, swimming in water, rowing a boat.

💡 Law of Conservation of Linear Momentum: When no external force acts on a system of interacting particles, the total linear momentum remains constant: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂.

title: Fundamental Rights & Constitutional Writs (Articles 12-35)
excerpt: 6 Fundamental Rights, Magna Carta of India, Article 32 vs 226, Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo-Warranto.
content:
1. Overview of Part III

Part III of the Constitution (Articles 12 to 35) is described as the Magna Carta of India. Originally there were 7 Fundamental Rights, but the Right to Property (Article 31) was deleted by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978 and made a legal right under Article 300A.

2. Six Fundamental Rights at a Glance

  • Right to Equality (Articles 14–18): Equality before law (14), Prohibition of discrimination (15), Equal opportunity in public employment (16), Abolition of Untouchability (17), Abolition of Titles (18).
  • Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22): Protection of 6 freedoms (19), Protection in conviction of offences (20), Protection of Life & Personal Liberty (21), Right to Education 6-14 yrs (21A - 86th Amdt), Protection against arrest/detention (22).
  • Right against Exploitation (Articles 23–24): Prohibition of human trafficking & forced labor (23), Prohibition of employment of children in hazardous industries (24).
  • Right to Freedom of Religion (Articles 25–28): Conscience and profession (25), Religious affairs (26), Tax exemption (27), Religious instruction (28).
  • Cultural & Educational Rights (Articles 29–30): Protection of minority interests (29), Right of minorities to establish educational institutions (30).
  • Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32): Dr. B.R. Ambedkar termed Article 32 as the "Heart and Soul of the Indian Constitution".

3. The Five Constitutional Writs

Supreme Court under Article 32 and High Courts under Article 226 can issue 5 types of writs:

1. Habeas Corpus (बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण): "To have the body of" — protects against unlawful detention.

2. Mandamus (परमादेश): "We Command" — orders a public official to perform statutory duties.

3. Prohibition (प्रतिषेध): Issued by higher court to lower court to prevent exceeding jurisdiction.

4. Certiorari (उत्प्रेषण): "To be certified" — quashes an order passed by a lower court/tribunal lacking jurisdiction.

5. Quo-Warranto (अधिकार पृच्छा): "By what authority" — enquires into legality of claim of a person to public office.

title: Work, Energy & Power
excerpt: Detailed notes on positive/negative/zero work, kinetic and potential energy formulas, mechanical energy conservation, and commercial power units.
content:
1. Scientific Definition of Work

Work is done only when a force causes displacement along or at an angle to the direction of force: W = F · d · cos(θ).

  • Positive Work (θ < 90°): Force and displacement in same general direction (e.g., pulling a toy car).
  • Negative Work (θ > 90°): Opposing force (e.g., Frictional force doing negative work on moving tires).
  • Zero Work (θ = 90° or d = 0): A coolie carrying luggage on his head walking horizontally does Zero work against gravity because the gravitational force is perpendicular to displacement (cos 90° = 0).

2. Energy & Conservation Principle

Energy is the capacity of doing work. Common forms in SSC syllabus:

  • Kinetic Energy (गतिज ऊर्जा): KE = ½ m v² = p² / (2m)
  • Gravitational Potential Energy (स्थितिज ऊर्जा): PE = m g h

🔥 SSC Numerical Shortcut: If the momentum of a body increases by 100%, its kinetic energy increases by 300%! (Because KE ∝ p²).

3. Commercial Unit of Electrical Energy

In electric utility billing, 1 Kilowatt-hour (1 kWh) is also known as 1 Board of Trade Unit (B.O.T.):

1 kWh = 1,000 Watts × 3,600 Seconds = 3.6 × 10⁶ Joules

title: Gravitation & Planetary Motion
excerpt: Newton's law of gravitation, variation of 'g' with altitude and depth, Kepler's laws, escape velocity, and artificial satellites.
content:
1. Universal Law of Gravitation

Every particle in the universe attracts every other particle with a force proportional to product of masses and inversely proportional to square of distance:

F = G · (m₁ · m₂) / r²

G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg² (Cavendish measured G using Torsion Balance).

2. Acceleration Due to Gravity (g)

Standard value at sea level: g = 9.8 m/s².

  • At Poles: 'g' is maximum (Earth is flattened at poles, smaller radius).
  • At Equator: 'g' is minimum.
  • At Earth's Center: 'g' is ZERO. Weight of an object at Earth's center is 0.
  • With Altitude (Height): 'g' decreases: g' ≈ g(1 - 2h/R).
  • With Depth: 'g' decreases: g' = g(1 - d/R).

3. Escape Velocity (पलायन वेग)

The minimum speed needed for an object to break free from Earth's gravitational pull without further propulsion:

v_e = √(2gR) = √(2GM/R) ≈ 11.2 km/s (for Earth)

For Moon, escape velocity is ~2.38 km/s (too low to hold gas molecules, hence Moon has no atmosphere!).
